title: Products are part of services

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Maya says her referral vanished. CarePath says it was sent. The clinic says it never arrived. Which screen would you redesign?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: I was going to make the status clearer. But I don't know what happened to the referral.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Good catch. Today we'll follow a product promise through the people, systems, and rules that must keep it. That's service design.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: All right. The doctor creates the referral. Then?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Secure transport sends it to an intake queue. Staff check eligibility and completeness. A clinician may triage it. Capacity determines the offer.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: And the notification is at the very end. A lovely status page can't make those earlier steps happen.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Where would you draw Maya on the map?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Above the line: what she does and waits through. On the line: the app, messages, and conversations she can see. Below it: queues, staff, policies, and data moving between systems.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Follow the referral itself. Where does it change state?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Wait. The intake system calls it returned, but CarePath only knows pending. No one recorded why it came back.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Now why is the message vague?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Because the service doesn't have a shared answer. Better copy alone would pretend to know more than it does.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: What needs to change besides the page?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Shared referral states, a reason for exceptions, staff access to the missing information, a real time expectation for Maya, and someone responsible when a referral stalls.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Do you own every operational process now?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: No. The blueprint makes the dependencies visible so clinical, operations, policy, and engineering can decide together.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Exactly. A customer sees one experience even when our organisation sees separate teams. Next we'll test whether a proposed improvement helps that whole experience.
